summary: Frontend-only verification of the Caracas (UTC-4) timezone fix. Container browser confirmed as TZ=UTC. Validated that timestamps stored in UTC render as UTC-4 in the DOM via the shared helper src/utils/dateFormat.js. Verified 3 primary surfaces: (1) Settings → Historial de Correos (email-logs) — raw '2026-07-23T01:02:07+00:00' rendered as '22/07/2026, 09:02 p. m.' (5/5 matches present in DOM). (2) ProjectDetail bitácora — raw '2026-07-14T01:35:06+00:00' rendered as '13/07/2026, 09:35 p. m.' (present in DOM). (3) Bell/notifications timestamps also render via the same helper (same DOM patterns confirmed). Format is exactly dd/mm/aaaa hh:mm a. m./p. m. with no TZ label, and every timestamp is exactly 4 hours less than the raw UTC value. No regression: date-only strings (YYYY-MM-DD) are handled by formatDate() without TZ conversion (day is preserved). Numeric toLocaleString formatting is untouched by the helper (no impact on HistoricalQuotes / KPIs).
critical_code_review_comments: dateFormat.js: parseUTC only appends 'Z' when the string matches HAS_TIME regex; strings like an ISO with fractional seconds and no offset (e.g. '2026-07-14T01:35:06.880439') still match HAS_TIME so are correctly treated as UTC — OK.
In InboxCenter.jsx there is a local formatDate(iso) wrapping the imported formatDateTime — cosmetic shadowing but not a bug (works as intended for showing dd/mm/aaaa hh:mm).

TallerEquipos.jsx, InventoryAccountingReport.jsx and AssetLedgerReport.jsx still define their own local formatDate/formatDateTime helpers (not migrated). They currently operate on report/purchase dates that appear to be date-only or backend-normalized dates, so no user-visible bug detected during this iteration; however for consistency and to prevent future regressions the main agent may consider migrating them to the shared helper as well.

Integrators.jsx keeps its own formatTimelineDate() for the integrator timeline entries; the field 'date' returned by the timeline endpoint should be reviewed — if it is a full ISO datetime (UTC) it will render in browser TZ (UTC), not Caracas. Recommend main agent verify and migrate to formatDate/formatDateTime.

AssetLedgerReport.jsx imports formatDateTime from '../utils/dateFormat' but then RE-DECLARES a local `const formatDateTime = (iso) => { ... return formatDateTime(d); }` at line 64 — this shadows the import and creates an infinite recursion / TDZ hazard when that local is invoked. Since Asset Ledger movements (mv.date) call this shadowed function, this file WILL crash the report if a mv.date is ever rendered. Report to main agent to fix (rename local or remove it and use the imported one).

success_rate.frontend: 100% for the timezone fix scenarios tested

context_for_next_testing_agent: Browser container runs in UTC. Helper /app/frontend/src/utils/dateFormat.js forces timeZone='America/Caracas'. Login endpoint POST /api/auth/login returns { session_token, user }; store token in localStorage under 'session_token' (and mirror to 'token','access_token','authToken' for safety). Endpoints used for verification: GET /api/email-logs?limit=N (Settings Historial), GET /api/notifications?limit=N (bell), GET /api/projects/{id} (bitacora key = 'bitacora'). Compare rendered DOM text against `new Date(raw_iso).toLocaleString('es-VE',{timeZone:'America/Caracas',day:'2-digit',month:'2-digit',year:'numeric',hour:'2-digit',minute:'2-digit',hour12:true})` — must match exactly. Follow-up items above (esp. AssetLedgerReport.jsx shadowed formatDateTime recursion) require attention.
rca of the issue: N/A — this iteration verified the fix, no bug reproduced. The fix (forcing timeZone 'America/Caracas' in Intl formatting and treating naive-with-time strings as UTC) is effective and consistent across Settings/email-logs, ProjectDetail bitácora, and notifications.
